newsitem.title: USA: Clinton surgery went well, doctors say.
newsitem.headline: Clinton surgery went well, doctors say.

text.p: President Bill Clinton came through emergency surgery to repair a torn knee tendon with no complications on Friday and doctors were "very pleased" with outcome, the White House said.

"No complications were reported to me," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters at Bethesda Naval Hospital. He said the doctors at that point were sewing up the incision in Clinton's damaged right knee and "were very pleased with the surgery and with the outcome."

McCurry said at 4:36 p.m. EST (2136 GMT) that the finishing touches would be completed in 10 to 15 more minutes and the president would enter post-operative care. He was expected to be taken to his hospital suite where his wife Hillary and daughter Chelsea were waiting for him.

The spokesman said Clinton "remained alert throughout it, but he apparently dozed off a few times." He had a "regional" anaesthetic, numbing him approximately from the mid-section down, and the White House said Constitutional procedures for shifting authority temporarily to Vice President Al Gore were not necessary.
Clinton caught his heel on a step at the Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman early on Friday, tearing the quadriceps tendon connecting the kneecap to the upper thigh in his right leg.
The emergency surgery was designed to reattach the tendon to the knee and it was expected Clinton would remain in the hospital at least until Saturday and possibly Sunday, doctors said.
